citations.quote: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering North Carolina A&T State University, Greensboro, NC, United States

In this direction, we present a model-based Concept of Operation (ConOps) for an ISC system using visible light communication (VLC). The ConOps model captures the scope definition process and the allocation of stakeholder requirements to stakeholder use cases. Also captured is the Operation Concept (OpsCon) and operational scenarios necessary for defining the system requirements.

This traditional approach suffers from: a lack of precision in describing system characteristics and operational scenarios, inconsistencies between related documents whose information are used in the preparation of the ConOps and difficulty in maintaining synchronization and consistency between stakeholder requirements and system level requirements.

It provides an efficient way to explore, update, and communicate system aspects to the stakeholders while significantly reducing or eliminating dependence on textual documents. Furthermore, explicit traceability between elements of the ConOps is achieved enabling better assessments of the impacts due to changes.

Outlined in this ConOps model is the baseline strategy for relay communications between three formation flying spacecrafts deployed in low earth orbit. The network of spacecrafts comprise two (2) CubeSats (6U) and One (1) SmallSat.

An MBSE framework for developing consistent ISC system architectures was developed in [7]. The activity diagram depicted in Fig. 3 outlines the major activities involved in the system scope definition process.
Based on the outcome of the need definition process, the goal of the project is to: "Develop a VL Hybrid Inter-Satellite Communication System that can be deployed on Small Satellite Systems"

The proposed Relay Communication System use cases include: Data Relay Services Use Case; Navigation Services Use Case and Timing Services Use Case. Each use case is associated with a use case description which is an informative statement that describes the scope of the use case. The Navigation Service and Timing Services use case descriptions are outside the scope of this work.
The iterative nature of the modeling process enables additional identified requirements be added and the model updated.

The System context and high-level operational behavior (nominal, alt-nominal and off-nominal scenarios) are captured in a model-centric way through the use of block definition diagrams, internal block diagrams, use case diagrams, use case mission statements and behavior (sequence) diagrams.

The Relay Communication Subsystem external interfaces include: Electrical Power Supply (EPS) system, Structural/Mechanical Support, Computer System, Flight Software, Communication Software, Transponder (of Twin CubeSat), Thermal Subsystem, On-board Storage Subsystem and System Operator (Commands).
Once the relay session is concluded the system enters into a standby state to conserve spacecraft power.

A verification, validation and test plan is created during the OpsCon definition activity. The plan created at this phase of conceptual development outlines activities that will need to be performed and the requirements for each activity [17] [18].
